title: Indistinguishability floor: a constant structural score cannot separate an orbit of equally plausible owners
author: Joseph Bingham
work: When Concealed Links Cannot Be Recovered: A Structural Identifiability Bound and Evaluation Pitfalls in Offshore Leak Networks
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 4.1 (source label 'thm:floor'), the indistinguishability floor of the paper's structural identifiability analysis: for a target entity whose stabiliser acts on the orbit of the true owner, every structural scoring rule is constant along that orbit, so ranking the true owner against a uniformly random orbit member has expected ROC-AUC exactly one half and the probability that the true owner is ranked strictly first is at most the reciprocal of the orbit size. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is not a numerical computation but a symmetry argument about identifiability: it transports an arbitrary pair of orbit members by a stabiliser element that fixes the target, applies isomorphism invariance of the scoring rule to show that the score is constant on the orbit, and then converts that constancy into the two quantitative evaluation consequences, namely the exact chance-level AUC and the tie-based bound on the top-one probability. Deriving an information-theoretic impossibility statement from group-theoretic invariance and drawing the evaluation consequences for a deployed scoring pipeline is research-level work in structural identifiability, beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
